And what the word of this is has been said, as I at least think; and the pillars of the long and broad courts he variegates with another word. With silver from head unto feet he says they must be very well glorified, yet again fixed upon bronze and silver-around bases. And a type

title: Silver light / bronze sound = gospel; oil for perpetual lamps
english: Cyril: …of this also would be Christ, because he has shone through in the manner of light, flashing with intelligible rays as God—the silver signifying. And that bright and well-sounding is the word about earth made for him—that is, the Gospel preaching—the silver-around bronze sideways hints to us. For well-sounding also is the bronze, and very bright and transparent is the matter of the silver. And this is in the Gospel preachings, and one would look down upon the Savior’s word, having the clear and pure of piety unto the extreme, and as buzzing around the whole inhabited world. And if someone should choose to pattern the holy apostles and evangelists as somehow in such pillars, he will reckon the likely things. For they are truly as silvered, through having become in a share of Christ who illuminates. Therefore he says: ‘And the brightness of the Lord our God will be upon us.’ (Psalm 90:17) And they are also named ‘Light of the world,’ (Isaiah 52:7) all but also having stepped in silver-around bronze. For a support for them is as to use the bright and most well-sounding word. ‘For the Lord,’ (Exodus 27:20–21) he says, ‘will give a word to those evangelizing with much power.’ (Matthew 5:14) And beautiful also are the feet of those evangelizing the goods, it has been written.
Palladius: Deep is the word, yet near truth.

Cyril: The things oracled upon the courts having then also been concluded, he turns unto construction of oil and myrrh and indeed also incense, saying thus: ‘And you, arrange for the sons of Israel; and let them take for you oil from olives, unpressed, pure, beaten unto light to burn, that a lamp may burn through all in the tent of the testimony, outside the veil that is upon the covenant, and Aaron and his sons will burn it from evening until morning before the Lord, an age-long lawful thing unto your generations, from the sons of Israel.’ (Psalm 68:11)
Palladius: And what then is this?

Cyril: It has a most necessary showing, and I say the riddle is wise; for with seven lamps, always burning and shining in the holy tent, one must very well liken the illumination through Christ, holding sufficiently unto being able to shine and kindle, or fill, the mind of those believing. For the number unto seven somehow hints everywhere the showing of perfection. As at least in saying somehow, ‘And a barren woman bore seven’ (1 Samuel 2:5)—that is, both most and as many as must be unto self-sufficiency. And Aaron and the remaining priests after him kindle the lamps. For as unquenchable the illumination from Christ is kept in Churches by the fairnesses of those allotted to be priests, who with initiations unto uprightness make bright the mind of those believing. For this, I think, is the lamps being kindled from evening until morning. And I think darkness is the wandering from the devil, and as somehow an intelligible night happening according to mind for humans—the
translator_notes: Ends mid-sentence into §29 heretics’ dark myths.

title: Pure olive oil = true doctrine; light outside veil for us
english: Cyril: …unholy heretics’ lightless and dim little myths. So then continuous and unending would the Savior’s light be seen in Churches, the teachers in them interpreting uprightly the divine and Gospel preachings. And pure is the oil; for as of lees and of every dirt the upright and true and unmixed-with-the-worse word about the divine dogmas has been altogether released, which always raises the Savior’s illumination—not itself adding something from home unto brightness for Christ (for altogether silly is thinking him to need a human), but because Christ, existing as the true light and radiance of the Father, with the teachers’ words unto uprightness appears to the understandings of those believing as what he truly is.
Palladius: And why does he say the oil is from olives? Therefore the very exact of the word perhaps travails something of the necessary contemplations.

Cyril: You think most excellently, and I will say what has come unto mind. It is not from olives alone, O Palladius, customary for those wise in these things to prepare the need of the oil, but also from however many other bastard and more earthy seeds. And the genuine will truly be from the most tested olives, and somehow counterfeit is what is as from force and craft, and as somehow not true—what is from the more earthy seeds, I mean. So then to the uncounterfeit and true word, also supplied through the wisdom from above to the worthy, one must very well liken the oil from olives. Yet what has been found from human notions and a demonic breathing-in is what is from certain ones’ craft and retail, and has a bastard use. And useless and cast-away is such a word, and altogether unprofitable unto illumination of the knowledge of Christ. Therefore also unacceptable in Churches, having neither the fragrant of the holy Spirit (‘For no one says, Lord Jesus, except in holy Spirit’ (1 Corinthians 12:3)), nor yet the genuine and unmuddied of the truth, and necessary unto useful benefit. And observe that the law says the oil from olives must be brought forward from the sons of Israel. For as I said having anticipated, a fruit will be from us and a spiritual gift-bearing to God—a true word, not allowing the illumination from Christ to be weak in those being initiated. And outside the veil is both the placement of the lamps and indeed also the burning. For Christ, existing as light according to nature, does not need light, but into us ourselves who are outside divinity, inasmuch as generated, he sends his own light. And as more inward than the veil was the ark, lying unto a patterning and image of Christ.
Palladius: You have spoken well.

Cyril: Then he says: ‘And the Lord spoke toward Moses: And you take spices, flower of chosen myrrh five hundred shekels, and of fragrant cinnamon the half of this, two hundred fifty, and of fragrant reed (Hebrews 1:3) (Exodus 30:22–25)

title: Holy anointing oil = Spirit in Christ; only God sanctifies; priests beyond flesh
english: Cyril: …two hundred fifty, and of iris five hundred shekels of the holy, and oil from olives will be, and you will make it oil—a holy anointing, a myrrh-working myrrh by craft of a myrrh-worker. It will be oil of holy anointing. And you will anoint from it the tent of the testimony, and the ark… and Aaron and his sons you will anoint, and you will sanctify them to priest for me… Upon flesh of a human it will not be anointed, and according to this composition you will not make likewise for yourselves… Whoever should make likewise, and whoever should give from it to an other-born, will be utterly destroyed from his people.’ So then of quality, and indeed also of composition, and again of inequality unto weight, I mean, of the named kinds, I would have nothing to say; for truth is dear to those accustomed to think well. And oil mixed with myrrhs would mark, as I at least think, the sanctification in Christ through Spirit supplied to those who have been pitied. According at least to the, ‘You fattened my head with oil.’ (1 Corinthians 4:7) And the tent is anointed, and all the things in it, for a place also would share sanctification through the one dwelling in it. And the vessels are also sanctified, according at least to the manner fitting for them, because useful for God’s liturgies, and the one touching them will be sanctified. So then untouchable for those still profane are the holy and sacred things; ‘For what communion of light toward darkness?’ (Exodus 30:22–33) according to what has been written. And he altogether forbids needing to make for yourselves the like construction of oil. For sanctifying is private of God alone, and as truly exceptional the matter will lie up for him, and for a generated and made nature—how would being able to sanctify others ever hold? For it is scarcely enriched with the sanctification from a share from above. And it would be fitting for it to be called upon through a voice of the holy ones. ‘For what do you have which you did not receive?’ (Psalm 23:5) And John also says concerning the Only-begotten that ‘From his fullness we all received.’ (John 1:16) And, ‘He does not give the Spirit from measure,’ (2 Corinthians 6:14) but rather existing himself as a spring of sanctification, he measures out the Spirit to the worthy, and sanctifies the rational creation; ‘And upon flesh of a human,’ (John 3:34) he says, ‘it will not be anointed,’ (Matthew 23:9) though having commanded Aaron and those priesting with him needing to be anointed from it. So then already beyond human is the holy race, inasmuch as also a sharer of Christ who is beyond the creation. Therefore also leading us up toward the dignity beyond nature, and as cutting us off from the earthly, he assigns us to the upper; ‘Father,’ he says,

title: No earthly father-title; holy to dogs ban; incense recipe = Christ alone
english: Cyril: …‘do not call yours upon the earth; for one is your Father, the one in the heavens, and all you are brothers.’ (Matthew 23:8–9) And destruction is the judgment for those providing from it to an other-born; ‘For do not give,’ (2 Corinthians 2:14) he says, ‘the holy things to the dogs, nor cast your pearls before the pigs.’ (Matthew 7:6) For bringing forward carelessly to those still unbelieving the hidden things, and the things fitting for holy ones alone, is full of danger; for what is still profane and sick extraordinarily with the uncleanness is not sanctified, but what has already been cleansed through the holy baptism.
Palladius: Truly.

Cyril: According to this equal manner and word he was also patterning the construction of the incense, saying: ‘And you take for yourself sweet things, drop and onyx, and galbanum of sweetening, and translucent frankincense, equal to equal it is, and they will make for it myrrh-working incense; a work of a myrrh-worker mixed, pure, a holy work… According to this composition it will not be made for you yourselves… Whoever should make likewise, so as to smell in it, will be destroyed from his people.’ (Exodus 30:34–38) And the word upon this again hints for us that the things exceptionally private are beyond all nature. And none of the made things shares them essentially, and nothing is altogether common for the creation toward the maker and master, as far as concerns a word of dignity and superiority of honors. And we will also remember having said both the gold altar, and the compound and thin incense itself, are Christ, and Emmanuel himself is marked for us through both. So then the incense being referred unto Christ (for incomparably fragrant), we will not make for ourselves according to that incense itself. For we will receive altogether no other upon him—just as indeed also the wretched Jews, the son of lawlessness. For such ones will be caught having compounded for themselves, and according to that fragrant and truly exceptional incense of the God and Father, who has made apparent for us the smell of his knowledge in the Son, through whom we also are fragrant—not having compounded the thin incense for ourselves, but as sharers of the incense, and anointed with the grace of the Spirit, and being eager to be well-reputed through the way of life in Christ.
Palladius: Through all then, as it seems, of what has become in the holy tent, the mystery of our Savior is patterned for us.
Cyril: And in addition to this you would also marvel, if you should learn that even the craftsmen of the holy tent themselves mold Christ, as at least in themselves.
Palladius: In what manner do you say? For I am not able to think.
Cyril: For it has been written again: ‘And the Lord spoke toward Moses, saying: Behold, I have called by name Bezalel the son of Uri, son of Hur of the (Exodus 31:1–2)

title: Bezalel = Christ from Judah; Eliab = apostles; Amen
english: Cyril: …tribe of Judah, and I filled him with divine Spirit of wisdom and understanding and knowledge. And in every work to understand the gold, and the silver, and the bronze, and the hyacinth, and the purple, and the spun scarlet, and the twisted linen, and the stone-works, and unto the carpenter works of the woods to work according to all the works. And I have also given him, and Eliab of Ahisamach, from tribe of Dan, and to every understanding heart I have given understanding, and they will make all things whatever I have arranged.’ Look then already how Bezalel leads the craft-works, and Eliab works.
Palladius: What then is this at least?

Cyril: You will learn then already; Judah and Dan, both from Jacob, but the one from the free woman Leah, and the other from the maidservant Bilhah. So then a type also clear is Bezalel of Christ who has appeared for us from tribe of Judah according to flesh, and from a nature truly free—clearly the divine and uppermost. And Eliab would hint very well those who have worked with Christ as from the slave woman Jerusalem—apostles and evangelists; for they have become fellow-workers of God all but laboring and crafting the things unto constitution of the holy Churches. And all the understanding in heart were bringing together the things from their own eagerness and fairness unto the works of the tent, fulfilling images of the teachers according to times, for whom in eagerness and care is working the things of God, and whatever would finish unto benefit of the Church of Christ; to him the glory unto the ages of the ages, Amen (Exodus 31:1–6) (Hebrews 7:14) (Galatians 4:22–26) (1 Corinthians 3:9).
translator_notes: Book 9 CLOSEOUT 32/32; OET; Melito skipped; never Cyril Matthew.
